level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in

short_summary.description: Compressed label for compact UI (≤60 chars): the claim alone, no rationale or consequence clause

category.description: Short kebab-case slug of the finding type, e.g. "correctness", "simplification", "efficiency", "test-coverage"

verdict.description: Set when a verify pass ran; absent on inline-only reviews

outcome.description: Set ONLY when re-reporting after applying fixes: what happened to this finding

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

# Atira starter kit

A minimal starting point, not an agent. It does the platform plumbing: it reads the run, attaches to the run's
browsers and shows how to call the free hosted models. Then it stops at `solve()` in `agent.py`, the place for your
agent. Out of the box it exits without an answer.

| File | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `run.py` | The run contract: reads the run (`load_run`) and submits an API answer (`submit_answer`) |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers over CDP and gets a page (`connect`); locally it starts a Chromium |
| `models.py` | One call to each hosted model: `ask_qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) and `ask_clef` (Cloudflare Clef) |
| `agent.py` | The entry point: reads the run, connects browser 1, calls `solve(task, page)` and submits what it returns |
| `agent.json` | How the sandbox installs (`uv sync`, the versions in `uv.lock`) and runs it; it waits for the hosted `qwen` |
| `tests/` | The plumbing against fakes |

`solve(task, page)` gets the run and a Playwright page in browser 1:

- `task["brief"]`: the task and its rules;
- `task["access"]`: each website's `siteId`, `url` and `credentials`;
- `task["submission"]`: where the answer goes, `{"kind": "api", "url": ...}` or `{"kind": "site", "url": ...}`;
- `task["answer_schema"]`: the JSON Schema of the answer.

For an `api` submission, return the answer and `main()` submits it: `202` is accepted and final, `400` lists the
issues to fix. For a `site` submission, enter the answer on that website yourself and return `None`. Reading pages,
acting on them and working out the answer are yours to build.

Mind the clock: a scored run has 20 minutes, and `run.seconds_left(task)` says how many seconds are left. Every part
of the answer scores on its own, so submit your best answer about a minute before the end rather than keep

"""The blackboard: the one place agents share data. Evidence goes in with its source; results are named values.

Everything is JSON-serialisable so a board can be dumped to `.swarm/` and replayed in local development.
Single event loop, so no locks; `wait_for` lets a downstream agent start as soon as upstream posts.
"""
import asyncio
import json
import time
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path


@dataclass
class Evidence:
    kind: str            # free-form label agreed between producer and consumer, e.g. "tender.position" (see docs/SWARM.md)
    site: str            # siteId the fact came from
    data: dict           # the extracted facts, as found (no interpretation)
    source: str = ""     # URL / document / mail subject: where exactly it was read
    author: str = ""     # agent name
    note: str = ""       # caveats: superseded? withdrawn? timezone? uncertain?
    ts: float = field(default_factory=time.time)


class Blackboard:
    def __init__(self):
        self.evidence: list[Evidence] = []
        self.results: dict = {}      # named outputs: "quantities", "materials", "prices", "bid", "answer", ...
        self.errors: list[dict] = []
        self._changed = asyncio.Condition()

    async def post(self, item: Evidence) -> None:
        async with self._changed:
            self.evidence.append(item)
            self._changed.notify_all()

    def query(self, kind: str | None = None, site: str | None = None, prefix: bool = False) -> list[Evidence]:
        def match(e: Evidence) -> bool:
            if kind is not None and not (e.kind.startswith(kind) if prefix else e.kind == kind):
                return False
            return site is None or e.site == site
        return [e for e in self.evidence if match(e)]

    async def set(self, key: str, value) -> None:
        async with self._changed:
            self.results[key] = value
            self._changed.notify_all()

    def get(self, key: str, default=None):
        return self.results.get(key, default)

    async def wait_for(self, kind: str | None = None, key: str | None = None, timeout: float = 600):
        """Block until evidence of `kind` exists (returns the list) or result `key` is set (returns it)."""
        def ready():
            if key is not None and key in self.results:
                return self.results[key]
            if kind is not None and self.query(kind):
                return self.query(kind)
            return None
        async with self._changed:
            await asyncio.wait_for(self._changed.wait_for(lambda: ready() is not None), timeout)
        return ready()

    def error(self, agent: str, message: str) -> None:
        self.errors.append({"agent": agent, "error": message, "ts": time.time()})

    def to_json(self) -> dict:
        return {"evidence": [asdict(e) for e in self.evidence], "results": self.results, "errors": self.errors}

    def dump(self, path: Path) -> None:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(self.to_json(), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1, default=str), encoding="utf-8")

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Path) -> "Blackboard":
        raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        board = cls()
        board.evidence = [Evidence(**e) for e in raw.get("evidence", [])]
        board.results = raw.get("results", {})
        board.errors = raw.get("errors", [])
        return board
EOF

"""Agent base class and registry. One agent = one file in `agents/`, registered with @register."""
import enum
import logging
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod


class Phase(enum.IntEnum):
    COLLECT = 1   # scrapers: read the sites, post Evidence
    ANALYZE = 2   # analyzers: turn evidence into structured facts (quantities, requirements, candidate materials...)
    VERIFY = 3    # verifiers: cross-check authority / dates / tender reference / superseded records
    COMPUTE = 4   # calculators: deterministic arithmetic, set results["bid"]
    SUBMIT = 5    # fills the configurator, signs; ALWAYS runs, with reserved time


REGISTRY: list[type["Agent"]] = []


def register(cls):
    REGISTRY.append(cls)
    return cls


class Agent(ABC):
    name: str = ""            # defaults to the class name
    phase: Phase = Phase.COLLECT
    browser: int | None = None   # index of the browser this agent drives (0-3), None = no browser
    uses_clef: bool = False

    def __init__(self, ctx):
        self.ctx = ctx
        self.name = self.name or type(self).__name__
        self.log = logging.getLogger(self.name)

    @abstractmethod
    async def run(self) -> None:
        """Read from `self.ctx.board`, do the work, write Evidence / results back. Raise on failure (it is logged;
        other agents carry on). Stop early when `self.ctx.time_left() <= 0`."""
EOF

"""Model access for agents: concurrency-limited, usage-counted, JSON-friendly. Qwen by default (hosted, free)."""
import asyncio
import json
import re

import models


def parse_json(text: str):
    """The first JSON object/array in a model reply (tolerates ``` fences and chatter)."""
    text = re.sub(r"^```(?:json)?|```$", "", text.strip(), flags=re.M).strip()
    for opener, closer in (("{", "}"), ("[", "]")):
        start, end = text.find(opener), text.rfind(closer)
        if start != -1 and end > start:
            try:
                return json.loads(text[start:end + 1])
            except ValueError:
                continue
    raise ValueError(f"no JSON in model reply: {text[:200]}")


class LLM:
    def __init__(self, max_concurrent: int = 24):
        self._sem = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)   # team limit is 32 concurrent Qwen calls
        self._client = None
        self.calls = 0
        self.tokens = {"prompt": 0, "completion": 0}

    @property
    def client(self):
        self._client = self._client or models.qwen()
        return self._client

    async def chat(self, messages: list[dict], *, tools: list[dict] | None = None, model: str = models.QWEN_MODEL,
                   **kwargs):
        """One chat completion; returns the message (`.content`, `.tool_calls`)."""
        args = dict(model=model, messages=messages, **kwargs)
        if tools:
            args["tools"] = tools
        async with self._sem:
            reply = await self.client.chat.completions.create(**args)
        self.calls += 1
        if reply.usage:
            self.tokens["prompt"] += reply.usage.prompt_tokens or 0
            self.tokens["completion"] += reply.usage.completion_tokens or 0
        return reply.choices[0].message

"""The blackboard: the one place agents share data. Evidence goes in with its source; results are named values.

Everything is JSON-serialisable so a board can be dumped to `.swarm/` and replayed in local development.
Single event loop, so no locks; `wait_for` lets a downstream agent start as soon as upstream posts.
"""
import asyncio
import json
import time
from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path


@dataclass
class Evidence:
    kind: str            # free-form label agreed between producer and consumer, e.g. "tender.position" (see docs/SWARM.md)
    site: str            # siteId the fact came from
    data: dict           # the extracted facts, as found (no interpretation)
    source: str = ""     # URL / document / mail subject: where exactly it was read
    author: str = ""     # agent name
    note: str = ""       # caveats: superseded? withdrawn? timezone? uncertain?
    ts: float = field(default_factory=time.time)


class Blackboard:
    def __init__(self):
        self.evidence: list[Evidence] = []
        self.results: dict = {}      # named outputs: "quantities", "materials", "prices", "bid", "answer", ...
        self.errors: list[dict] = []
        self._changed = asyncio.Condition()

    async def post(self, item: Evidence) -> None:
        async with self._changed:
            self.evidence.append(item)
            self._changed.notify_all()

    def query(self, kind: str | None = None, site: str | None = None, prefix: bool = False) -> list[Evidence]:
        def match(e: Evidence) -> bool:
            if kind is not None and not (e.kind.startswith(kind) if prefix else e.kind == kind):
                return False
            return site is None or e.site == site
        return [e for e in self.evidence if match(e)]

    async def set(self, key: str, value) -> None:
        async with self._changed:
            self.results[key] = value
            self._changed.notify_all()

    def get(self, key: str, default=None):
        return self.results.get(key, default)

    async def wait_for(self, kind: str | None = None, key: str | None = None, timeout: float = 600):
        """Block until evidence of `kind` exists (returns the list) or result `key` is set (returns it)."""
        def ready():
            if key is not None and key in self.results:
                return self.results[key]
            if kind is not None and self.query(kind):
                return self.query(kind)
            return None
        async with self._changed:
            await asyncio.wait_for(self._changed.wait_for(lambda: ready() is not None), timeout)
        return ready()

    def error(self, agent: str, message: str) -> None:
        self.errors.append({"agent": agent, "error": message, "ts": time.time()})

    def to_json(self) -> dict:
        return {"evidence": [asdict(e) for e in self.evidence], "results": self.results, "errors": self.errors}

    def dump(self, path: Path) -> None:
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(self.to_json(), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1, default=str), encoding="utf-8")

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, path: Path) -> "Blackboard":
        raw = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        board = cls()
        board.evidence = [Evidence(**e) for e in raw.get("evidence", [])]
        board.results = raw.get("results", {})
        board.errors = raw.get("errors", [])
        return board

"""Model access for agents: concurrency-limited, usage-counted, JSON-friendly. Qwen by default (hosted, free)."""
import asyncio
import json
import re

import models


def parse_json(text: str):
    """The first JSON object/array in a model reply (tolerates ``` fences and chatter)."""
    text = re.sub(r"^```(?:json)?|```$", "", text.strip(), flags=re.M).strip()
    for opener, closer in (("{", "}"), ("[", "]")):
        start, end = text.find(opener), text.rfind(closer)
        if start != -1 and end > start:
            try:
                return json.loads(text[start:end + 1])
            except ValueError:
                continue
    raise ValueError(f"no JSON in model reply: {text[:200]}")


class LLM:
    def __init__(self, max_concurrent: int = 24):
        self._sem = asyncio.Semaphore(max_concurrent)   # team limit is 32 concurrent Qwen calls
        self._client = None
        self.calls = 0
        self.tokens = {"prompt": 0, "completion": 0}

    @property
    def client(self):
        self._client = self._client or models.qwen()
        return self._client

    async def chat(self, messages: list[dict], *, tools: list[dict] | None = None, model: str = models.QWEN_MODEL,
                   **kwargs):
        """One chat completion; returns the message (`.content`, `.tool_calls`)."""
        args = dict(model=model, messages=messages, **kwargs)
        if tools:
            args["tools"] = tools
        async with self._sem:
            reply = await self.client.chat.completions.create(**args)
        self.calls += 1
        if reply.usage:
            self.tokens["prompt"] += reply.usage.prompt_tokens or 0
            self.tokens["completion"] += reply.usage.completion_tokens or 0
        return reply.choices[0].message

    async def ask(self, system: str, user: str, **kwargs) -> str:
        message = await self.chat([{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}], **kwargs)
        return message.content or ""

Subclass, set `site_id` and `browser`, and write `goal()` (what the model should find, in general terms derived from
the brief; never scenario values). Override `run()` if you need several browse passes (e.g. one per sub-task).

from swarm.agent import Agent, Phase
from swarm.blackboard import Evidence
from swarm.browser_agent import browse


class SiteScraper(Agent):
    phase = Phase.COLLECT
    site_id: str = ""
    max_steps: int = 40
    hints: str = ""

    def goal(self) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def login_text(self) -> str:
        site = self.ctx.site(self.site_id)
        return f"Site {self.site_id}: {site['url']}  credentials: {site.get('credentials')}"

    async def post(self, rec: dict) -> None:
        await self.ctx.board.post(Evidence(kind=rec["kind"], site=self.site_id, data=rec["data"],
                                           source=rec["source"], author=self.name, note=rec["note"]))

    async def run(self) -> None:
        page = await self.ctx.pool.new_page(self.browser or 0)
        try:

                               site_id=self.site_id, on_record=self.post, max_steps=self.max_steps,
                               hints=self.hints, author=self.name)
            await self.ctx.board.set(f"{self.name}.summary", out["summary"])
            self.log.info("done in %d steps, %d records: %s", out["steps"], len(out["records"]), out["summary"][:200])
        finally:
            await page.close()

"""Runs the registered agents phase by phase. Agents of one phase run concurrently; a failing agent never stops others.

Time: non-SUBMIT phases are cut off when the useful time is gone (ctx.time_left() <= 0), then SUBMIT always runs.
Local dev: SWARM_ONLY=a,b runs only those agents; SWARM_BOARD_IN=.swarm/board.json preloads a saved board (ignored
in scored runs). The board is dumped to .swarm/board.json after every phase.
"""
import asyncio
import importlib
import logging
import os
import pkgutil
from pathlib import Path

import agents as agents_pkg
from swarm.agent import REGISTRY, Agent, Phase
from swarm.blackboard import Blackboard
from swarm.browser_pool import BrowserPool
from swarm.context import Context
from swarm.llm import LLM

log = logging.getLogger("swarm")
BOARD_DUMP = Path(".swarm/board.json")


def discover() -> list[type[Agent]]:
    """Import every module in agents/ so its @register decorators run."""
    for mod in pkgutil.iter_modules(agents_pkg.__path__):

"""Base class for site scrapers: a model-driven browse of ONE site that streams Evidence onto the blackboard.

Subclass, set `site_id` and `browser`, and write `goal()` (what the model should find, in general terms derived from
the brief; never scenario values). Override `run()` if you need several browse passes (e.g. one per sub-task).
"""
from swarm.agent import Agent, Phase
from swarm.blackboard import Evidence
from swarm.browser_agent import browse


class SiteScraper(Agent):
    phase = Phase.COLLECT
    site_id: str = ""
    max_steps: int = 40
    hints: str = ""

    def goal(self) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def login_text(self) -> str:
        site = self.ctx.site(self.site_id)
        return f"Site {self.site_id}: {site['url']}  credentials: {site.get('credentials')}"

    async def post(self, rec: dict) -> None:
        await self.ctx.board.post(Evidence(kind=rec["kind"], site=self.site_id, data=rec["data"],
                                           source=rec["source"], author=self.name, note=rec["note"]))

    async def run(self) -> None:
        page = await self.ctx.pool.new_page(self.browser or 0)
        try:
            out = await browse(self.ctx, page, f"{self.login_text()}\n\nBRIEF:\n{self.ctx.brief}\n\nYOUR JOB:\n{self.goal()}",
                               site_id=self.site_id, on_record=self.post, max_steps=self.max_steps,
                               hints=self.hints, author=self.name)
            await self.ctx.board.set(f"{self.name}.summary", out["summary"])
            self.log.info("done in %d steps, %d records: %s", out["steps"], len(out["records"]), out["summary"][:200])
        finally:
            await page.close()

"""Your agent's entry point: agent.json runs `uv run --no-sync python agent.py`, in the sandbox and on your machine.

The kit only does the plumbing: run.py reads the run and submits an answer, browsers.py attaches to the run's
browsers, models.py calls the hosted Qwen and Clef. Everything else is yours to build, in `solve` below.
Docs: $API/docs/building-an-agent.md, $API/docs/run-contract.md, and the rules: $API/docs/fair-play.md
"""
import asyncio
import json
import sys

import logging

from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

import run as contract
from swarm.orchestrator import run_swarm


async def solve(task: dict, playwright, scored: bool) -> dict | None:
    """Runs the swarm (see docs/SWARM.md). Agents live in agents/; the orchestrator runs them phase by phase.

    For an "api" submission the swarm leaves the answer in board.results["answer"]; for a "site" submission the
    submit agent enters it on the website and the result is None.
    """
    return await run_swarm(task, playwright, scored)


async def main() -> int:
    logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(name)s %(message)s")
    task, token = contract.load_run()
    sites = ", ".join(f"{site.get('siteId')} {site.get('url')}" for site in task["access"])
    print(f"Run {task.get('run_id') or '(local: the scouting logins, nothing counts)'}; websites: {sites}; "
          f"answer via {task['submission']['kind']}", flush=True)
    async with async_playwright() as playwright:
        answer = await solve(task, playwright, scored=bool(token))
    if answer is None:
        print("No answer to submit: build your agent in solve() in agent.py", flush=True)
        return 0
    if not token:
        print("Your answer (locally nothing is submitted):", json.dumps(answer, ensure_ascii=False), flush=True)
        return 0
    status, body = contract.submit_answer(task, token, answer)
    print(f"Answer: HTTP {status} {body[:2000]}", flush=True)
    return 0 if status == 202 else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(asyncio.run(main()))

"""The swarm framework against fakes: blackboard, JSON parsing, phase orchestration, failure isolation."""
import asyncio
import sys
import time
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import patch

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))

from swarm import Agent, Blackboard, Evidence, Phase  # noqa: E402
from swarm import orchestrator  # noqa: E402
from swarm.llm import parse_json  # noqa: E402

TASK = {"brief": "b", "access": [{"siteId": "erp", "url": "http://x", "credentials": {}}],
        "submission": {"kind": "site"}, "expires_at": None}


class BoardTests(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def test_post_query_and_wait(self):
        board = Blackboard()
        waiter = asyncio.create_task(board.wait_for(kind="a.b", timeout=2))
        await asyncio.sleep(0)
        await board.post(Evidence("a.b", "erp", {"x": 1}, source="u"))
        self.assertEqual((await waiter)[0].data, {"x": 1})
        self.assertEqual(len(board.query("a", prefix=True)), 1)
        self.assertEqual(board.query("a.b", site="mail"), [])

    async def test_dump_and_load_round_trip(self):
        board = Blackboard()
        await board.post(Evidence("k", "erp", {"x": 1}))
        await board.set("r", [1])
        path = Path(__file__).parent / "_board.json"
        try:
            board.dump(path)
            again = Blackboard.load(path)
        finally:
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        self.assertEqual(again.evidence[0].data, {"x": 1})
        self.assertEqual(again.get("r"), [1])


class ParseJson(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_fenced_and_chatty(self):
        self.assertEqual(parse_json('Sure!\n```json\n{"a": [1, 2]}\n```'), {"a": [1, 2]})

    def test_garbage_raises(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            parse_json("no json here")


def make_agents(order):
    class Boom(Agent):
        phase = Phase.COLLECT
        async def run(self): raise RuntimeError("boom")

    class Collect(Agent):
        phase = Phase.COLLECT
        async def run(self):
            order.append("collect")
            await self.ctx.board.post(Evidence("k", "erp", {}))

    class Analyze(Agent):
        phase = Phase.ANALYZE
        async def run(self):
            order.append(f"analyze sees {len(self.ctx.board.query('k'))}")

    class Submit(Agent):
        phase = Phase.SUBMIT
        async def run(self):
            order.append("submit")
            await self.ctx.board.set("answer", {"ok": True})

    return [Submit, Analyze, Boom, Collect]


class Orchestration(unittest.IsolatedAsyncioTestCase):
    async def run_with(self, classes, task=TASK, env=None):
        with patch.object(orchestrator, "discover", lambda: classes):
            return await orchestrator.run_swarm(task, None, scored=True, env=env or {})

    async def test_phases_run_in_order_and_a_failure_does_not_stop_the_rest(self):
        order = []
        answer = await self.run_with(make_agents(order))
        self.assertEqual(order, ["collect", "analyze sees 1", "submit"])
        self.assertEqual(answer, {"ok": True})

    async def test_only_filter(self):
        order = []
        await self.run_with(make_agents(order), env={"SWARM_ONLY": "Collect,Submit"})
        self.assertEqual(order, ["collect", "submit"])

    async def test_out_of_time_skips_work_but_still_submits(self):
        order = []
        late = {**TASK, "expires_at": (time.time() + 10) * 1000}   # inside the submit margin
        answer = await self.run_with(make_agents(order), task=late)
        self.assertEqual(order, ["submit"])
        self.assertEqual(answer, {"ok": True})


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Swarm guide

One process, one asyncio loop, many agents. Agents share a **blackboard**; the **orchestrator** runs them in phases.
Each person owns **one file in `agents/`** (no merge conflicts); shared code is in `swarm/` (change it by PR, small).

```
COLLECT (scrapers, 1 per site, own browser) -> ANALYZE -> VERIFY -> COMPUTE (plain code) -> SUBMIT (always runs)
        post Evidence                           read board, write results[...]                 enter bid + sign TAN
```

## Files

| Path | What |
| --- | --- |
| `swarm/blackboard.py` | `Evidence(kind, site, data, source, author, note)`, `Blackboard` (post/query/set/get/wait_for/dump/load) |
| `swarm/agent.py` | `Agent` base, `Phase`, `@register` |
| `swarm/context.py` | `ctx`: `task`, `board`, `llm`, `pool`, `site(id)`, `brief`, `time_left()`, `seconds_left()` |
| `swarm/llm.py` | `ctx.llm.chat / ask / ask_json` (Qwen, concurrency-limited, usage counted), `parse_json` |
| `swarm/browser_agent.py` | `browse(ctx, page, goal, ...)`: model-driven browser loop (goto/click/fill/select/record/finish) |
| `swarm/scraper.py` | `SiteScraper`: subclass, set `site_id`, `browser`, write `goal()` |
| `swarm/orchestrator.py` | discovery of `agents/*`, phases, timeouts, failure isolation, board dumps |
| `agents/*.py` | the agents. Header comment of each file: OWNER / ROLE / NEEDS / WRITES |

Starting agents (all stubs except the 4 scrapers, which run a generic goal): `scrape_tender`, `scrape_spec`, `scrape_erp`,
`scrape_mail`, `analyze_quantities`, `analyze_requirements`, `analyze_materials`, `analyze_discount`, `verify_evidence`,
`compute_bid`, `submit_bid`. Add a new agent = add a file with `@register` (nothing else to wire).

## Adding / changing an agent

```python
@register
class MyAgent(Agent):
    phase = Phase.ANALYZE
    async def run(self):
        positions = self.ctx.board.query("tender.position")        # list[Evidence]
        out = await self.ctx.llm.ask_json("system...", "user...")   # model decides; code validates
        await self.ctx.board.set("quantities", out)                 # named result for downstream agents
```
Need an extra browser tab: `page = await self.ctx.pool.new_page(self.browser)` (max 4 browsers: indices 0-3; tabs unlimited).
Need an upstream result within the same phase: `await self.ctx.board.wait_for(key="requirements", timeout=...)`.
Always check `self.ctx.time_left()` in loops. Raise on failure: it is logged on `board.errors`, others carry on.

## Contracts (agree before changing)

Evidence `kind` names (producer -> consumer): `tender.meta|position|clarification`, `spec.revision|requirement|amendment`,
`erp.material|stock|price_condition|other`, `mail.discount_approval|tan|other`. Keep `data` = facts as shown on the page
(strings as found, with dates and sender), interpretation happens in analyzers. Put caveats in `note`.
Results keys: `quantities`, `requirements`, `materials`, `discount`, `verification`, `bid`, `answer`. **Document the shape of
each result you write at the top of your agent file** so consumers can rely on it; change shapes only after telling the consumer.
If your upstream data is missing, degrade (partial bid) rather than crash: a signed partial bid beats nothing.

## Local development

```powershell
atira models proxy                                   # terminal 1
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression   # terminal 2
uv run --no-sync python agent.py                     # whole swarm; dumps .swarm/board.json after each phase
$env:SWARM_ONLY="MaterialMatcher"; $env:SWARM_BOARD_IN=".swarm/board.json"
uv run --no-sync python agent.py                     # only your agent, on a saved board (no re-scraping)
uv run --no-sync python -m unittest discover -s tests -q
```
`SWARM_BOARD_IN` is ignored in scored runs. `.swarm/` holds scouting data: git-ignored, never ship it.
Agents can be unit tested with a `Context(task, Blackboard(), fake_llm, None)`; see `tests/test_swarm.py`.

## Fair-play rules for everyone (a reviewer reads the package)

- No scenario values anywhere (prices, material numbers, refs, logins, TANs, totals, dates): not in prompts, defaults, tests or notes.
  Tests use invented dummy data. Strategy ("latest approval for this exact tender wins") is fine, values are not.
- The model decides where to go and what matters. Code may parse, page through model-selected results, validate, compute.
  Do not write fixed click paths, URL lists, or crawl-everything-then-one-prompt helpers.
- Only the provided CDP browsers; no extra Chromium; no hosts besides the platform and the 4 sites; models via the proxy.
- Do not write comments addressed to the reviewer.

## Not yet done (first tasks)

- `browse()` is untested against the real sites (the Playwright driver does not start in the dev sandbox): first scout run
  will need prompt/observation tuning (iframes, popups, ERP transaction codes). Owner of each scraper tunes their `goal()`/`hints`.
- Submit fallback timer: SUBMIT phase runs only after earlier phases end or time out at `time_left() <= 0`
  (75 s margin before expiry); the submitter must finish inside that margin or enter progressively.
- agent.json `"browsers": 4` is not set yet (scrapers use browsers 0-3); add it when the scrapers go to a test run.
- Token/cost budget per agent is not tracked yet (only totals in `ctx.llm`).

The swarm framework is in place and the 21 unit tests pass. None of it has run against the real sites yet, because Playwright's driver wouldn't start in this sandbox. The model-driven browsing loop is the part most likely to need tuning on the first scout run.

Nothing is committed. `agent.py` now just calls the orchestrator, so the starter's `solve(task, page)` is gone.

## How it works
- **One process, many agents.** Agents share a blackboard and run in five phases: COLLECT (scrapers), ANALYZE, VERIFY, COMPUTE and SUBMIT. Agents within a phase run concurrently, and a crash in one is logged without stopping the others.
- **Each person owns one file in `agents/`.** Adding an agent means adding a file with `@register`; the orchestrator finds it automatically.
- **The blackboard** holds `Evidence` records (kind, site, data, source, note) and named `results`. Agents can wait on each other with `board.wait_for(...)`.
- **Shared helpers** are in `swarm/`. `ctx.llm` is a concurrency-limited Qwen client with JSON parsing and retry. `ctx.pool.new_page(n)` opens a tab in one of the 4 run browsers. `ctx.time_left()` is the run clock.
- **`browse()` is the shared browsing loop.** The model chooses the navigation. The loop gives it page text plus numbered elements, and the actions goto, click, fill, select, press, `record` and `finish`. `record` streams facts to the board as it finds them.
- **`SiteScraper`** is the base class for scrapers. A subclass sets `site_id` and `browser` and writes a `goal()` in general terms.

## Starting agents
- **Scrapers (working, generic goals):** `scrape_tender`, `scrape_spec`, `scrape_erp` and `scrape_mail`, on browsers 1–4. `agent.json` now sets `"browsers": 4`.
- **Stubs with their inputs and outputs in the header:** `analyze_quantities`, `analyze_requirements`, `analyze_materials`, `analyze_discount`, `verify_evidence`, `compute_bid` and `submit_bid`.
- Each file has an `# OWNER:` line to fill in.

## Time handling
- Phases before SUBMIT stop 180 s before expiry.
- SUBMIT always runs and is cut off 60 s before expiry.

## Local dev tools
- `SWARM_ONLY=AgentName` runs just your agent.
- `SWARM_BOARD_IN=.swarm/board.json` replays a saved board, so analyzers don't have to re-scrape.
- The orchestrator dumps the board to `.swarm/` after each phase. That folder is git-ignored and the replay is ignored in scored runs.

## Other changes
- `tests/test_kit.py` now uses a fake Playwright. Three entry-point tests failed on the unmodified repo because the driver can't start here.
- `docs/SWARM.md` has the contracts, the dev workflow and the fair-play rules.
- `CLAUDE.md` has a one-line pointer to it. `pytest` isn't installed, so I ran the tests with `python -m unittest discover -s tests`.

- **Evidence kinds and result keys.** I proposed names in `docs/SWARM.md`, such as `tender.position`, `erp.material` and `results["quantities"]`. The team should agree on them before anyone relies on them.

message.content: what framework is used? Explain in simple words.

content.text:
No existing agent framework (LangGraph, CrewAI and so on) is used. It's a small custom one I wrote, built on plain Python:

- **`asyncio`** runs many agents at the same time in one program.
- **Playwright** controls the browsers.
- **The OpenAI SDK** calls the hosted Qwen model.

## The idea: a shared whiteboard

Think of a team in one room with a whiteboard:

1. **Scrapers** go to the four websites (tender, spec, ERP, mail). Whenever they find a fact, they write it on the whiteboard with where they found it.
2. **Analyzers** read the whiteboard and work things out, such as "what is the final quantity for each position?" or "which ERP material matches?" They write their conclusions back.
3. **Verifiers** double-check those conclusions, for example the sender, the tender reference and superseded records.
4. **The calculator** is plain code with no AI. It computes prices and rounding exactly.
5. **The submitter** takes the finished bid, fills in the website form and signs it.

The whiteboard is the `Blackboard` class. The "manager" that decides who works when is the orchestrator. It runs the phases in order and starts every agent in a phase at the same time. If one agent crashes, the others carry on. It also makes sure the submitter always gets time before the deadline.

## How a scraper uses the AI

The AI (Qwen) is given the page text and a numbered list of buttons and links. It picks the next action each step: click, type, go to a URL, save a fact, or finish. The code only carries out those actions. This keeps us within the rule that the model, not a fixed script, chooses where to go.

## Why each person gets one file

Every agent is one file in `agents/`. Add the `@register` marker and the orchestrator finds it automatically. Teammates work in separate files, so they don't create merge conflicts for each other.

I chose this over a ready-made framework for three reasons:
- It stays small and easy to read.
- It follows the contest rules, including the 4-browser limit, the proxy and the time limit.
- It lets us avoid learning and debugging a big library during a hackathon.

You can still use another framework inside your own agent file if you want to. It must use the provided browsers and model proxy.

"""Model-driven browsing via the browser-use framework. The MODEL decides where to go and what matters; browser-use gives
it hands and eyes. This module only wires it to our setup: the run's CDP browsers, the Qwen proxy, no telemetry, navigation
limited to the task's websites, and a `record` action that streams facts onto the blackboard.

    out = await browse(ctx, goal="...", browser=1, site_id="erp", on_record=callback)

Rule: ONE browse() at a time per browser index (an agent works in the browser's active tab). Use different indices (0-3)
for parallel agents. Per-site knowledge goes into `goal`/`hints` as general strategy, never scenario values.
"""
import logging
import os
from urllib.parse import urlparse

# No telemetry / cloud sync / version check: the sandbox may only talk to the platform and the four sites.
for _flag in ("ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY", "BROWSER_USE_CLOUD_SYNC", "BROWSER_USE_VERSION_CHECK"):
    os.environ[_flag] = "false"
os.environ.setdefault("BROWSER_USE_LOGGING_LEVEL", "info")

from browser_use import ActionResult, Agent, BrowserProfile, BrowserSession, ChatOpenAI, Tools  # noqa: E402
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field  # noqa: E402

import browsers  # noqa: E402
import models  # noqa: E402

log = logging.getLogger("browse")

SYSTEM_EXTRA = """
Working rules:
- Dismiss cookie walls/popups; if a session expired, log in again (credentials are in the task); retry flaky error pages.
- Watch for traps: look-alike or superseded records, paging, hidden tabs/iframes, archive folders, other timezones.
- Call `record` for every relevant fact as soon as you see it, copied exactly as shown. Never invent values.
- Finish with `done` and a short summary when the goal is met or you are stuck."""


class RecordParams(BaseModel):
    kind: str = Field(description="what this fact is, e.g. a label agreed with the analyzers")
    data: dict = Field(description="the facts exactly as shown on the page")
    source: str = Field(default="", description="URL / document / mail subject where it was read")
    note: str = Field(default="", description="caveats: superseded, withdrawn, other timezone, unsure")


def allowed_domains(task: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Only the task's websites may be opened (fair play: no other hosts)."""
    out = []
    for site in task.get("access", []):
        parts = urlparse(site.get("url") or "")
        if parts.netloc:
            out.append(f"{parts.scheme}://{parts.netloc}")
    return out


def make_llm() -> ChatOpenAI:
    """The hosted Qwen through the proxy. Settings tuned for a non-OpenAI model; adjust here if tool calls misbehave."""
    return ChatOpenAI(model=models.QWEN_MODEL, base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
                      temperature=0.0, frequency_penalty=None, timeout=360, max_retries=3,
                      add_schema_to_system_prompt=True, dont_force_structured_output=True,
                      remove_min_items_from_schema=True, remove_defaults_from_schema=True)


def make_session(ctx, browser: int = 0) -> BrowserSession:
    """Attach to the run's CDP browser `browser` (locally browser-use starts its own Chromium; HEADLESS=1 hides it)."""
    urls = browsers.cdp_urls()
    profile = dict(allowed_domains=allowed_domains(ctx.task), enable_default_extensions=False, keep_alive=True)
    if urls:
        return BrowserSession(cdp_url=urls[browser % len(urls)], **profile)
    return BrowserSession(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1", **profile)


async def browse(ctx, goal: str, *, browser: int = 0, site_id: str = "", on_record=None, max_steps: int = 40,
                 hints: str = "", author: str = "browse", use_vision="auto") -> dict:
    """Run a browser-use agent until done / max_steps / out of time. Returns {"summary", "records", "steps", "done"}."""
    records: list[dict] = []
    tools = Tools()

    @tools.action("Save a fact you found (kept even if you run out of time). Use for every relevant fact.",
                  param_model=RecordParams)
    async def record(params: RecordParams, browser_session: BrowserSession):
        url = await browser_session.get_current_page_url()
        rec = {"kind": params.kind, "data": params.data, "source": params.source or url, "note": params.note,
               "site": site_id, "author": author}
        records.append(rec)
        if on_record:
            await on_record(rec)
        return ActionResult(extracted_content=f"recorded {params.kind}")

    session = make_session(ctx, browser)
    agent = Agent(task=goal, llm=make_llm(), browser_session=session, tools=tools, use_vision=use_vision,
                  use_judge=False, generate_gif=False, extend_system_message=SYSTEM_EXTRA + (f"\n{hints}" if hints else ""))

    async def stop_when_out_of_time(_agent) -> None:
        if ctx.time_left() <= 0:
            agent.stop()

    try:
        history = await agent.run(max_steps=max_steps, on_step_start=stop_when_out_of_time)

it hands and eyes. This module only wires it to our setup: the run's CDP browsers, the Qwen proxy, no telemetry, navigation
limited to the task's websites, and a `record` action that streams facts onto the blackboard.

    out = await browse(ctx, goal="...", browser=1, site_id="erp", on_record=callback)

Rule: ONE browse() at a time per browser index (an agent works in the browser's active tab). Use different indices (0-3)
for parallel agents. Per-site knowledge goes into `goal`/`hints` as general strategy, never scenario values.

import logging
import os
from urllib.parse import urlparse

# No telemetry / cloud sync / version check: the sandbox may only talk to the platform and the four sites.
for _flag in ("ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY", "BROWSER_USE_CLOUD_SYNC", "BROWSER_USE_VERSION_CHECK"):
    os.environ[_flag] = "false"
os.environ.setdefault("BROWSER_USE_LOGGING_LEVEL", "info")

from browser_use import ActionResult, Agent, BrowserProfile, BrowserSession, ChatOpenAI, Tools  # noqa: E402
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field  # noqa: E402

import browsers  # noqa: E402
import models  # noqa: E402

log = logging.getLogger("browse")

SYSTEM_EXTRA = """
Working rules:
- Dismiss cookie walls/popups; if a session expired, log in again (credentials are in the task); retry flaky error pages.
- Watch for traps: look-alike or superseded records, paging, hidden tabs/iframes, archive folders, other timezones.
- Call `record` for every relevant fact as soon as you see it, copied exactly as shown. Never invent values.
- Finish with `done` and a short summary when the goal is met or you are stuck."""


class RecordParams(BaseModel):
    kind: str = Field(description="what this fact is, e.g. a label agreed with the analyzers")
    data: dict = Field(description="the facts exactly as shown on the page")
    source: str = Field(default="", description="URL / document / mail subject where it was read")
    note: str = Field(default="", description="caveats: superseded, withdrawn, other timezone, unsure")


def allowed_domains(task: dict) -> list[str]:
    """Only the task's websites may be opened (fair play: no other hosts)."""
    out = []
    for site in task.get("access", []):
        parts = urlparse(site.get("url") or "")
        if parts.netloc:
            out.append(f"{parts.scheme}://{parts.netloc}")
    return out


def make_llm() -> ChatOpenAI:
    """The hosted Qwen through the proxy. Settings tuned for a non-OpenAI model; adjust here if tool calls misbehave."""
    return ChatOpenAI(model=models.QWEN_MODEL, base_url=os.environ["QWEN_BASE_URL"], api_key=os.environ["QWEN_API_KEY"],
                      temperature=0.0, frequency_penalty=None, timeout=360, max_retries=3,
                      add_schema_to_system_prompt=True, dont_force_structured_output=True,
                      remove_min_items_from_schema=True, remove_defaults_from_schema=True)


def make_session(ctx, browser: int = 0) -> BrowserSession:
    """Attach to the run's CDP browser `browser` (locally browser-use starts its own Chromium; HEADLESS=1 hides it)."""
    urls = browsers.cdp_urls()
    profile = dict(allowed_domains=allowed_domains(ctx.task), enable_default_extensions=False, keep_alive=True)
    if urls:
        return BrowserSession(cdp_url=urls[browser % len(urls)], **profile)
    return BrowserSession(headless=os.environ.get("HEADLESS") == "1", **profile)


async def browse(ctx, goal: str, *, browser: int = 0, site_id: str = "", on_record=None, max_steps: int = 40,
                 hints: str = "", author: str = "browse", use_vision="auto") -> dict:
    """Run a browser-use agent until done / max_steps / out of time. Returns {"summary", "records", "steps", "done"}."""
    records: list[dict] = []
    tools = Tools()

    @tools.action("Save a fact you found (kept even if you run out of time). Use for every relevant fact.",
                  param_model=RecordParams)
    async def record(params: RecordParams, browser_session: BrowserSession):
        url = await browser_session.get_current_page_url()
        rec = {"kind": params.kind, "data": params.data, "source": params.source or url, "note": params.note,

    async def stop_when_out_of_time(_agent) -> None:

    finally:
        await session.kill() if not browsers.cdp_urls() else await session.stop()   # never kill the run's browsers

content.text:
I replaced the custom browsing loop with browser-use and kept our orchestrator and shared blackboard. The 22 unit tests pass. I haven't run a full browse against a real site or the Qwen proxy.

**What changed**
- **Dependencies:** `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` now include `browser-use`. I also added `pydantic-settings`, because browser-use 0.11.13 imports it without declaring it, and `import browser_use` failed until I did.
- **`swarm/browser_agent.py`:** this is now the only place that touches browser-use. `browse(ctx, goal, browser=n, ...)` does the following:
  - **Attach:** it connects to the run's CDP browser number `n`. It doesn't launch its own browser in a run; locally it starts one.
  - **Qwen:** it calls Qwen through the proxy. The settings are a first guess for a non-OpenAI model: schema in the prompt, no forced structured output, no frequency penalty.
  - **Fair play:** telemetry, cloud sync and the version check are switched off, because each one calls an outside host. Navigation is limited to the task's site URLs, and the extension download is off.
  - **`record` action:** the model can call it to save a fact. The fact goes onto the blackboard immediately, so it survives a timeout.
  - **Time limit:** the run stops when the useful time is gone.
- **`SiteScraper`** now calls `browse()`. The four scrapers on browsers 1–4 work as before.
- **`docs/SWARM.md`** has a new browser-use section and the rule to run one `browse()` per browser at a time.

**Checked**
- The telemetry flags read as off.
- `allowed_domains` has a test.
- A browser-use `Agent` builds with our Qwen client and CDP session.

**Needs doing on the first scout run**
- Qwen's tool-call format may need tuning in `make_llm()`. The first run will show.
- I never ran the scrapers or the `record` action against a live site or the model, so that is the first thing to try.
- The analyzers, verifier, calculator and submitter stubs are unchanged. The analyzers and verifier don't need browser-use; they use `ctx.llm`.

I haven't committed anything.

Yes, you can test the four scrapers now. Everything after them is a stub, so no run will produce an answer yet. A run will exit with "No answer to submit". That is fine for now, because the goal is to check that browsing works and facts reach the blackboard.

## 1. Local run (free, unscored, fastest feedback)

Terminal 1:
```powershell
atira models proxy
```
Terminal 2:
```powershell
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
uv run playwright install chromium      # once
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```
- To test one scraper, set `$env:SWARM_ONLY="MailScraper"` first. The names are `TenderScraper`, `SpecScraper`, `ErpScraper` and `MailScraper`.
- Watch the console for browser-use's step log (actions, errors) and the swarm lines such as "done in N steps, M records".
- Open `.swarm/board.json` afterwards. If the Evidence entries hold real page content, with a source URL for each, the scraper works.
- If Qwen's tool calls fail, you'll see errors or repeated retries. The fix goes in `make_llm()` in `swarm/browser_agent.py`.

## 2. Check the package, then run it in the real sandbox

```sh
atira test-run . --dry-run      # what would be packed
atira test-run . --follow       # same sandbox as scored runs, public data, unscored, up to 2 h
```
The sandbox adds checks you don't get locally: the CDP browsers, `uv sync` from the lockfile, and the 4-browser setup. A test run can show things a local run can't, such as whether the sandbox blocks any browser-use network call.

Afterwards:
```sh
atira status
atira logs <reh_id> --follow
```
With the `atira` MCP server you can also ask Claude "why did run reh_xxx fail?". It can pull `diagnose_run`, `run_llm_calls` and `run_screenshot`, which is the easiest way to see what the model did on each site.

## What to look for
- Do all four sites log in, including the ERP after its short session timeout?
- Does each scraper post sensible Evidence?
- Do Qwen's tool calls parse reliably, or does browser-use loop on errors?

A real answer needs the stubs filled in. The order is: analyzers, then calculator, then submitter. Until then, test runs only prove the scraping layer.

Before the first test run, check the Python version. Your local venv is on 3.14, while CLAUDE.md says the sandbox uses 3.12. Dependencies resolved fine, but the test run is where any 3.12 difference would show.

entries.description: Why a run failed and what to do next, in one call: the failure class and whether a rerun as it is would help, the last 20 lines of stdout and stderr, the answer, model errors by status, stretches over 60 s with no input, no screen change and no model call, and browsers whose screen froze. About 2–3k tokens.

run_id.description: A run id (run_...) from list_runs, a test run id (reh_...), or a submission id (sub_...: its latest run)

entries.name: mcp__atira__get_run
entries.description: One run in full: status, phase and failure, its place in the queue or the free models' warm-up while it waits, phase starts on the run's clock, the package, LLM calls by model with failures and queue waits, the score with points per field (test runs), the recordings, the answer it entered, and the run page URL (?t=mm:ss opens the replay there). About 1–2k tokens.

run_id.description: A run id (run_...) from list_runs, a test run id (reh_...), or a submission id (sub_...: its latest run)

entries.name: mcp__atira__run_logs
entries.description: A run's log lines, in time order, each with its time on the run's clock and its stream. Streams: stdout and stderr (your agent system), setup (the platform: install, the free models' warm-up), input (what the browsers received; run_inputs reads them better, so they're left out unless you ask). Narrow with from/to (e.g. from 02:10 to 02:40), grep, browser; tail for the last lines; page with after. About 30 tokens a line.

run_id.description: A run id (run_...) from list_runs, a test run id (reh_...), or a submission id (sub_...: its latest run)

from.description: The earliest time, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

to.description: The latest time, on the run's clock, as the run page and run_logs show it: mm:ss or h:mm:ss (seconds may have a fraction), 3m20s, or seconds; a minus is before the start. An ISO 8601 time also works.

stream.description: Only these streams, comma-separated: stdout, stderr, setup, input; "all" is every one. Default: stdout, stderr and setup.

grep.description: Only lines containing this text, case-insensitive; a|b matches either

browser.description: Only the platform's lines about this browser (its inputs, a browser it stopped)

tail.description: Only the last n matching lines

after.description: Continue after a previous page: its `next` value

entries.name: mcp__atira__wait_for_run

"""Base class for site scrapers: a model-driven browse of ONE site that streams Evidence onto the blackboard.

Subclass, set `site_id` and `browser`, and write `goal()` (what the model should find, in general terms derived from
the brief; never scenario values). Override `run()` if you need several browse passes (e.g. one per sub-task).
"""
from swarm.agent import Agent, Phase
from swarm.blackboard import Evidence
from swarm.browser_agent import browse


class SiteScraper(Agent):
    phase = Phase.COLLECT
    site_id: str = ""
    max_steps: int = 40
    hints: str = ""

    def goal(self) -> str:
        raise NotImplementedError

    def login_text(self) -> str:
        site = self.ctx.site(self.site_id)
        return f"Site {self.site_id}: {site['url']}  credentials: {site.get('credentials')}"

    async def post(self, rec: dict) -> None:
        await self.ctx.board.post(Evidence(kind=rec["kind"], site=self.site_id, data=rec["data"],
                                           source=rec["source"], author=self.name, note=rec["note"]))

    async def run(self) -> None:
        out = await browse(self.ctx, f"{self.login_text()}

BRIEF:
{self.ctx.brief}

YOUR JOB:
{self.goal()}",
                           browser=self.browser or 0, site_id=self.site_id, on_record=self.post,
                           max_steps=self.max_steps, hints=self.hints, author=self.name)
        await self.ctx.board.set(f"{self.name}.summary", out["summary"])
        self.log.info("done in %d steps, %d records: %s", out["steps"], len(out["records"]), out["summary"][:200])

content.text:
The framework runs in the real sandbox and the goal of starting parallel development is met, so I cancelled the test run. I stopped it after about 2.5 minutes, so I haven't seen a scraper finish, and none posted a fact before I stopped it.

## What the run showed
- The first run failed in 4 seconds on my own bug. A broken f-string in `swarm/scraper.py` crashed the import. The unit tests missed it because they mocked agent discovery. I fixed it and added a test that imports every real agent module.
- The second run worked at the infrastructure level:
  - All 4 scrapers started in parallel on their own browsers.
  - Each logged in to its site (tender, customer portal, ERP, mail) and navigated, paging through the document register and getting past a dialog and the mail login.
  - Qwen calls went through the proxy: 29 calls, about $0.03 in 2 minutes.
  - Telemetry and other outside hosts caused no errors.

## Problems seen, and what to fix
1. **Qwen sometimes returns malformed JSON.** Three "Result failed 1/6" errors appeared in the first minute. browser-use retries up to 6 times, so it recovers, but it wastes calls. The fix is in `make_llm()` in `swarm/browser_agent.py`: try a prompt or output-format tweak, or set `fallback_llm`.
2. **No facts recorded yet.** The scrapers were still navigating, so I couldn't check whether the model calls `record`. Whoever tunes the scrapers should check this first.
3. **Speed.** Calls take about 10 s each at p50, and the ERP lands on a "notice/unlock" page that needs a receipt number. The ERP scraper owner will have to deal with that.
4. **The run clock shows 7198 s (2 h) in test runs.** The 20-minute limit only applies to scored runs, so test runs won't exercise the time cut-offs.

## Is the original goal done?
Yes, for splitting the team up:
- **Shared infrastructure** (`swarm/`) is working: blackboard, orchestrator, LLM helper, browser-use wiring.
- **One file per agent** in `agents/`, so people won't conflict.
- **The four scrapers** are real starting points, not stubs.
- **`docs/SWARM.md`** explains the contracts and the local dev loop.

Suggested assignments:
- **Scrapers:** one person per site, tuning each `goal()` against logs and `.swarm/board.json`.
- **Analyzers:** quantities, requirements, materials and discount. They can build against saved boards using `SWARM_BOARD_IN`.
- **Verifier, calculator and submitter:** one person each.

Two things still need doing:
- **Commit and push.** Nothing is committed, so teammates can't see any of this yet.
- **Agree the evidence kinds and result shapes** listed in `docs/SWARM.md`, so analyzers and scrapers match each other.

Do you want me to commit this?

@AGENTS.md

# Project guide: Atira EHL challenge agent ("From RFQ to bid")

A Python agent that, at run time, uses a model (hosted Qwen) to navigate four websites (tender portal, supplier portal,
ERP, webmail), work out the task from the brief, and submit one answer. Brief: `atira challenge rfq`.
Platform docs: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/start and `https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/docs/run-contract.md`.

## Layout

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `agent.py` | Entry point. Write the agent in `solve(task, page)`. |
| `run.py` | Run contract: `load_run`, `submit_answer`, `seconds_left`. Platform plumbing, change rarely. |
| `browsers.py` | Attaches to the run's browsers (CDP); locally starts Chromium. |
| `models.py` | `ask_qwen`, `ask_clef`, `qwen()` (OpenAI SDK client). |
| `agent.json` | Sandbox config: `setup`, `run`, `models` (hosted models to wait for), optional `"browsers": 1-4`. |
| `swarm/`, `agents/` | Agent-swarm framework and one file per agent: see `docs/SWARM.md` (read before adding an agent). |
| `tests/` | Unit tests against fakes. |

`task` has `brief`, `access` (site ids, URLs, credentials), `submission` (`api` or `site`) and `answer_schema`.
For `api` submissions return the answer from `solve()`; for `site` submissions enter it on the website and return `None`.

## Rules that decide whether a submission is accepted

- A model must pick navigation targets and make decisions at runtime. No hardcoded answers, fixed scripts, crawlers
  or copied values. A coding agent reviews every package. Helpers (parsing, pagination of a model-selected result set,
  validation, form filling) are fine.
- A scored run lasts 20 min. Submit the best answer about 1 min before the end (`run.seconds_left(task)`); late = 0.
- Max 4 browsers, 4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM. The sandbox only reaches the platform and the websites.
- Package: max 20 MB compressed, `agent.json` at the root. Never include `.env` or keys (they are git-ignored).
- Hosted models are free, but each call adds simulated cost to ranking (quality, then cost x time). Use Qwen for
  easy steps; first call after idle can take several minutes, so use long timeouts.

## Setup per laptop (once)

Prerequisites: Git, Python is NOT required (uv manages 3.12), and a GitHub account that is on the Atira team.

### Windows (PowerShell)
```powershell
irm https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.ps1 | iex          # Atira CLI (read the script first if you prefer)
winget install --id astral-sh.uv -e                           # uv
# open a NEW terminal so PATH updates
atira login                                                   # browser sign-in with GitHub
uv sync
uv run playwright install chromium
```

### macOS / Linux
```sh
curl -fsSL https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/install.sh | sh     # Atira CLI; then add ~/.local/bin to PATH
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh               # uv (or: brew install uv)
# open a NEW terminal
atira login
uv sync
uv run playwright install chromium        # on Linux add: uv run playwright install-deps chromium
```

### Both: Claude Code helpers (optional)
```sh
claude mcp add atira -- atira mcp     # lets Claude read run logs, model calls, timings, compare runs
```
Check with `atira whoami`. Use `atira login --device` if no browser is available.

## Develop locally

Two terminals, both in the repo root.

Terminal 1 (leave open): the free-model proxy.
```sh
atira models proxy
```

Terminal 2: load scouting env, then run the agent.
```powershell
# Windows PowerShell
atira scout --env | Out-String | Invoke-Expression
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```
```sh
# macOS / Linux
eval "$(atira scout --env)"
uv run --no-sync python agent.py
```
`atira scout --env` sets `CHALLENGE_SCOUTING`, `CHALLENGE_SITE_ACCESS`, site URLs and the `QWEN_*` / `CLEF_*`
variables pointing at the local proxy. The variables only live in that terminal. Local runs use the public
scouting logins: nothing done there is scored, and answers entered on the tender portal never count. Local model calls
are free and unranked. `atira scout` (no flag) prints the logins and brief for manual browsing.

Unit tests: `uv run --no-sync python -m pytest tests -q` (add pytest with `uv add --dev pytest` if missing).

## Test in the real sandbox

```sh
atira test-run . --follow        # same sandbox as scored runs, public dataset, up to 2 h, not ranked
atira test-run . --dry-run       # only shows what would be packed (no upload)
```
Max 3 test runs waiting at once. Inspect results:
```sh
atira status                     # latest submissions and test runs
atira logs <run-id> --follow     # reh_... (test run) or run_... (scored run)
atira package <id>               # what was uploaded
atira cancel <run-id>
```
With the `atira` MCP server Claude can also fetch logs by time, model calls, where time went, browser screens and
compare two runs. Ask it "why did run reh_xxx fail?".

## Submit (ranked, public)

Run a test run first and make sure it finishes with a valid answer. Then agree in the team who submits
(one submission in flight per team, and it is public and final).
```sh
atira submit . --dry-run         # check the package
atira submit . --follow          # review -> one scored run on the public dataset -> leaderboard
atira leaderboard
```
The final ranking uses a private dataset with different websites and data, so build a general agent that does not
rely on public-dataset specifics. Choose the final attempt with `atira final [--best-of 1|3]` before the final run
starts (own model keys cost up to 3x).

## Models

- Default: hosted `qwen` (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, up to 32 concurrent calls/team) via `models.qwen()`; `clef` (image
  decision model, 16 concurrent) via `models.ask_clef`. List every hosted model used in `agent.json` `"models"`.
- Own provider keys (Anthropic, OpenAI, ...) are stored as team secrets on the team page and go through the run's
  metering proxy. See the run contract, section LLM calls.
- Claude Code (this assistant) is only for writing code and runs on your own Claude. Optional experimental launcher
  `claude-atira` (Windows, per-user setup, not in the repo) points Claude Code at Qwen; plain `claude` is the default.

## Team workflow

- Commit with normal `git commit` / `git push` so Entire checkpoints get linked. Do not push `entire/*` branches.
- Never read, print or commit `.env` or API keys. `.entire/settings.json` is shared; `settings.local.json` is personal.
- Pull before starting, keep commits small, and say in the team chat before running `atira submit`.

## Challenge overview: `rfq` v6 (source: challenge page, fair-play.md, run-contract.md; checked 2026-10-10)

Goal: turn a public tender (German hydraulics manufacturer, hydraulic cylinders) into one correct, priced, **signed** bid
without human help. Answer is entered in the **tender-portal** configurator (`submission.kind = site`), signed with a TAN
from the webmail. Limits: answer 65,536 B, up to 100 positions, notes 4,000 chars.

### The four sites (each run has its own logins; public scouting logins are unscored)
| Site | Holds | Traps |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tender-portal` | tender, bill of quantities, bidder Q&A (changes quantities), bid configurator | cookie wall, flaky error pages, docs behind expression of interest, iframes, ZIPs, deadline in other timezone |
| `customer-portal` | buyer's technical spec + revisions | opens OLDEST revision first, nested viewers, paged tables |
| `erp` | materials, stock, lead times, price conditions | SAP-style transaction codes, F4 search popup, status codes, short session timeout (re-login) |
| `mail` | sales inbox: director's discount approval, signing TAN | look-alike/superseded approvals, archive folder, paging |

### Bid rules (29 in the brief; the brief in `task["brief"]` is authoritative, re-read it every run)
- Quantity = tender qty, overridden by the latest clarification per position; withdrawn answers ignored.
- Requirement = spec revision marked *current*, with scoped amendments applied.
- Material = active ERP material matching bore, stroke, pressure, mounting, certification EXACTLY; none -> "no bid".
- Price = valid price condition on scenario date at highest reached quantity scale, minus approved discount, round half-up
  to the cent, converted to EUR. Discount = latest sales-director approval for this exact tender (conditional thresholds), else 0%.
- Lead time = stock if it covers qty, else production lead time; shared stock is all-or-nothing per material.
- Konditionsgruppen decide if discount hits base only / base + mass surcharge / neither. Setup fees never discounted.
- Packaging cartons, shared setup/pool fees, delivery commitments allocated per position; project bonus = marginal
  percentage bands allocated proportionally in cents; final price formula rounds ONCE at the end.
- Metal-index rates selected by date; nominal stroke derived from reserves.
- Authority: only authorised senders + exact tender reference; newest valid record wins.
- Partial submission allowed (explicitly omitted positions) but bid must still be signed. Missing material -> no bid.

### Scoring / ranking
- Quality 0-100: decision 5, reference 5, discount 5, positions 75 (minus extra checks), total 5, arithmetic consistency 5;
  +5 each for withdrawn-quantity and metal-index checks when present. Per position: material 20%, quantity 15%,
  base price 15%, surcharge 10%, packaging 10%, project bonus 10%, final unit price 10%, delivery 10%.
- Correct tender reference is mandatory (else ineligible, ranked after all eligible).
- Order: eligible -> quality (higher) -> cost x time (lower; cost = simulated model prices, time = wall clock to accepted answer).
- Final ranking: PRIVATE dataset first, then public, then "system elegance". Private = same jobs/rules/format but different
  software, layouts, names, content, data. Do NOT tune to public-1; derive everything from the sites at runtime.
- Private run uses latest passing submission (or best of 3 if opted in via `atira final --best-of 3`).

### Fair play (an AI reviewer reads the whole package: passed / flagged / rejected)
Forbidden: any scenario value in the package (code, config, prompts, notes, defaults, fallbacks: prices, material numbers,
totals, discounts, tender refs, logins, TANs); pre-solving the answer (yourself or with an assistant) and shipping it;
fixed click paths; crawl-everything-then-one-model-call; model only as fallback; contacting hosts other than platform + 4 sites;
models outside the proxy; local/bundled models; starting own browsers (even headless; extras are killed); attacking platform/sites;
sharing scored-run data. Never write notes addressed to the reviewer (steering counts against us).
Allowed: any agent design, any provider via the proxy with team-secret keys, own code/prompts/tools, OSS libs installed in
`setup`, knowledge from scouting/test runs (as general strategy, never as values), helper code for browser control, parsing,
arithmetic, validation, retries, form filling, paging through results the model selected.
Helpers MAY NOT discover and traverse the sites to assemble evidence: the model decides where to go, what to search, what matters.

### Building an agent swarm
- Multiple agents/processes/threads are explicitly allowed; no limit on agent count, only **max 4 browsers** (`"browsers": n`
  in `agent.json`, CDP urls in `CDP_URLS`, browser n = display `:n`, CDP port 9221+n). Tabs/contexts inside them are unlimited.
- Frameworks: nothing is whitelisted or banned; any open-source library (respect licence) installed during `setup`
  (network allowed there, no credentials). Toolchains: Python 3.12 + uv, Node 24 (+pnpm, bun, runs .ts), Rust/cargo, gcc, make, git, curl, jq.
  Run phase is offline except platform + sites + model proxy. Package <= 20 MB. Plain asyncio/threads + OpenAI SDK is enough;
  agent frameworks (LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, smolagents, browser-use, etc.) are fine if they use the proxy base URLs
  and the provided CDP browsers (never launch their own Chromium in scored runs; connect via CDP).
- Suggested shape: an orchestrator (model) that reads the brief and spawns one worker per site / per position
  (tender, spec, ERP, mail run in parallel on separate browsers), workers return structured evidence with source + timestamps,
  a calculator step (plain code, deterministic rounding rules) computes prices, a verifier agent cross-checks authority/dates/
  tender reference/superseded records, then one agent fills the configurator and signs with the TAN.
- Models: hosted `qwen` (32 concurrent, 256k ctx, vision) for navigation/extraction; `clef` (16 concurrent) for quick
  choice/score decisions; use a stronger own-key model only for hard reasoning (cost x time only matters as tie-break after quality,
  so quality first). Every call counts simulated cost, so keep prompts short and use cached prefixes. Warm-up can take minutes: long timeouts.
  List hosted models in `agent.json` `"models"` (`[]` skips warm-up wait).
- All LLM traffic via `$LLM_PROXY_URL` / `<MODEL>_BASE_URL`; send your own User-Agent on platform HTTP calls (default Python UA gets 403).

### Run discipline
- Clock starts at the `run` command; scored 20 min; submit the best answer by ~1 min before end (`run.seconds_left`); late/no answer = 0.
- Build a fallback: keep a best-so-far answer and submit it on a timer even if the swarm is unfinished.
- Submission 400 with `issues` is not final (fix + resend); 202 is final and the process has 10 s to exit.
- Sessions time out (ERP, portals): handle re-login. Prefer partial-correct signed bid over nothing.
- Test runs (2 h, unscored) on public data first; use `atira` MCP (`diagnose_run`, `run_logs`, `run_llm_calls`, `run_profile`) to debug.
  Never copy values from logs/screenshots/answers into the package.

### Links
Challenge: https://ehl-challenge.atira.ai/challenges/rfq · fair play: /docs/fair-play.md · run contract: /docs/run-contract.md ·
API: /docs/api.md · CLI: /docs/cli.md · llms.txt: /llms.txt · leaderboard: /challenges/rfq/leaderboard.md

| `swarm/`, `agents/` | Agent-swarm framework and one file per agent: see `docs/SWARM.md` (read before adding an agent). |
| `tests/` | Unit tests against fakes. |

`task` has `brief`, `access` (site ids, URLs, credentials), `submission` (`api` or `site`) and `answer_schema`.
For `api` submissions return the answer from `solve()`; for `site` submissions enter it on the website and return `None`.

## Rules that decide whether a submission is accepted

- A model must pick navigation targets and make decisions at runtime. No hardcoded answers, fixed scripts, crawlers
  or copied values. A coding agent reviews every package. Helpers (parsing, pagination of a model-selected result set,
  validation, form filling) are fine.
- A scored run lasts 20 min. Submit the best answer about 1 min before the end (`run.seconds_left(task)`); late = 0.
- Max 4 browsers, 4 vCPU / 8 GB RAM. The sandbox only reaches the platform and the websites.
- Package: max 20 MB compressed, `agent.json` at the root. Never include `.env` or keys (they are git-ignored).
- Hosted models are free, but each call adds simulated cost to ranking (quality, then cost x time). Use Qwen for
  easy steps; first call after idle can take several minutes, so use long timeouts.
